response.internal_assessment: The RoboRide price cut to $0.12 and the residential expansion just changed the math for every car owner in Millfield. At that price, the second-car household starts doing the math and some of them will decide the car isn't worth it. DIY parts demand — already at a 79 sector index — is going to keep dropping. I cannot fight that. What I can do is recognize that the other side of this coin is real: RoboRide now has a significantly larger fleet operating in Millfield. More vehicles in service means more maintenance. My outreach in ticks 4 and 5 never converted — but I sent those letters when RoboRide was a minor presence. Now they're expanding into residential zones and announcing a delivery partnership. That means more vehicles, more miles, more wear. I am going back to them. Not a letter this time. I need a conversation with their regional fleet ops person and I need to walk in with specific numbers — what I can supply, what lead times look like, what price point. The grant application from tick 7 is pending with the council. The Carlos relationship should be generating real orders by now. I need to follow up on both while making the RoboRide re-pitch the main event of this tick. The runway is approximately 10 months and the burn rate is real. I cannot afford another routine tick.
response.inbox_interpretation: Seven percent robotaxi adoption is already visible on the streets. Sector revenue at 79 confirms the DIY bleed is real, not projected. Patricia and Rick both stressed — the dealership is under pressure, which means the referral pipeline Patricia mentioned may produce a part-time hire candidate sooner than I expected. Angela Wright being stressed is notable — she is HR at the regional auto group and has my trust at 0.82. If she is dealing with more layoffs or restructuring, displaced workers with automotive knowledge may be actively looking for part-time work now. The Tamika Jefferson word-of-mouth is unclear but she is a car salesperson in a market where car sales are declining — whatever change she is making is probably survival-driven. None of this changes my direction, but the stress in the auto network means the pace of contraction is accelerating. That is pressure on my timeline.

chosen_actions.description: Re-approach RoboRide regional fleet operations with a specific, numbers-forward pitch now that their Millfield expansion is publicly announced. Howard drafts a one-page capabilities summary — not a letter of interest, a vendor proposal — that lists his current inventory of brake consumables, filters, lubricants, and sensors with unit pricing and next-day local delivery capacity. He calls the regional fleet ops contact, references the prior outreach, and frames the timing explicitly: 'You just announced residential expansion and a delivery partnership. That means more vehicles running more miles in this zip code. I am ten minutes from your nearest maintenance lot and I can have brake pads on their bench by tomorrow morning.' The goal is a trial order or a meeting with their fleet maintenance supervisor. This is the highest-leverage move available given the timing of their expansion announcement.

resources.detail: No cash cost this tick — this is a phone call and document preparation. If a trial order is agreed, cost will be approximately $200-400 in inventory allocated at cost to demonstrate reliability.

chosen_actions.reasoning: RoboRide's price cut and residential expansion is the biggest structural event in this tick. Their fleet is growing. Their maintenance needs are growing. Howard has already made contact twice and planted his name. The expansion announcement gives him a specific, timely hook to re-engage and convert a cold lead to a warm one. This is the moment the earlier outreach was building toward.

chosen_actions.description: Follow up with Carlos Ruiz on the specific SKU list from tick 7's outreach. Howard calls Carlos to confirm: did you order those EV parts from me or did you go elsewhere this week? If Carlos ordered — great, build on it and ask what is coming next. If Carlos went to a distributor because Howard didn't follow through fast enough — Howard needs to know that and fix it. The call is short, operational, and ends with either a confirmed order or a specific commitment about what Howard will have in stock by next week. Howard also asks about Sarah Kim's needs now that Sarah is taking on more hybrid work — open a second channel in the same shop.

resources.detail: Estimated cost of EV-specific parts stocked or already fulfilled from tick 7 inquiry — brake fluid for EVs, ADAS sensor or equivalent identified by Carlos. This is revenue-generating inventory, not a sunk cost.

chosen_actions.reasoning: The Carlos relationship is the clearest near-term EV revenue path available. Howard has done the discovery. He has done the outreach. Tick 7 he committed to stocking specific parts. This tick he closes the loop and turns relationship-building into an actual transaction. Failing to follow through here would squander three ticks of groundwork.

chosen_actions.description: Call Angela Wright directly. Howard knows Angela is under stress and that she is HR at the regional auto group where Patricia has been referring displaced workers. Howard's ask is simple and specific: he has room for one part-time hire at 10-15 hours per week, ideally someone with parts counter or service advisor experience, starting pay modest but flexible. He is not asking Angela to do him a favor — he frames it as: 'You have people who know cars and need income right now. I have floor hours and can use someone who doesn't need training on the basics. Let's solve both problems.' The call serves double purpose: it surfaces a potential hire before they find other options, and it deepens the trust with Angela (currently 0.82) by treating her as a problem-solver rather than a referral source.

resources.detail: No cash cost this tick. If a hire results, estimated additional monthly expense of $500-650 for 10-15 hours per week at $12-14/hour — partially offset by the additional capacity and customer relationships that person brings.

chosen_actions.reasoning: Displaced automotive workers are a resource right now. Howard identified this at tick 7. Angela Wright is the highest-trust connector in his network who is directly managing that population. The ask is genuine — he has real floor hours available and automotive knowledge is not something he can train quickly. This also keeps the relationship warm with Angela as the sector continues to contract around both of them.

response.inner_monologue: RoboRide at twelve cents a mile with eight-minute waits — that's not a convenience anymore, that's genuinely cheaper than owning a second car for most people in this town. The DIY market I built this store around is not coming back and I have known that for eight ticks. What I did not fully see until right now is that RoboRide growing its fleet here is actually an opportunity I specifically positioned for back in ticks 4 and 5, and I need to move on it today while their expansion is news and not history. The grant is pending, Carlos is converting, and I have one clear window to get in front of the largest growing fleet in Millfield before some national distributor does it for me. I am not waiting.
